---
title: Add a new method
---

There are two situations: adding a method that exists from the start of the simulation, and
introducing one partway through, for example to represent a product launch.

## Which approach to use

The choice module has to know how likely women are to pick the new method, and how long
they stay on it. `SimpleChoice` and `StandardChoice` read that from per-method fitted data,
which a brand-new method does not have -- passing them an unknown method raises an
`IndexError` while processing durations.

So there are two workable routes:

- **`fp.add_method` with `copy_from`**, which inherits an existing method's behavior. This
  is the right choice for essentially all real analyses.
- **Building the method list directly**, which only works with `RandomChoice` unless you
  also supply the fitted data. `RandomChoice` allocates methods uniformly at random, so it
  is for testing mechanics, not for producing realistic method mix.

## Add a method from the start (testing only)

```python
import starsim as ss
import fpsim as fp
import fpsim.methods as fpm

methods = fpm.make_methods()  # Start from the default set
methods += fpm.Method(
    name     = 'dmpasc',
    label    = 'DMPA-SC',
    efficacy = 0.983,
    modern   = True,
    dur_use  = ss.lognorm_ex(ss.years(2), ss.years(1)),
)

sim = fp.Sim(location='kenya', contraception_module=fpm.RandomChoice(methods=methods))
sim.run()
```

## Introduce a method partway through (recommended)

The `fp.add_method` intervention adds a method at a given year, copying the uptake
behavior of an existing method. Pass the new method's attributes in `method_pars` and name
the method to copy switching behavior from in `copy_from`:

```python
import starsim as ss
import fpsim as fp

intv = fp.add_method(
    year        = 2010,
    copy_from   = 'inj',  # Inherit switching behavior from injectables
    method_pars = dict(
        name     = 'dmpasc',
        label    = 'DMPA-SC',
        efficacy = 0.983,
        dur_use  = ss.lognorm_ex(ss.years(2), ss.years(1)),
    ),
)

sim = fp.Sim(location='kenya', interventions=intv)
sim.run()
```

`copy_from` takes the method's `name`, not its label. You can also pass a fully-specified
`fp.Method` object as `method=` instead of using `method_pars`.

By default the new method adds to total use. To have it instead take share from the method
it was copied from, use `split_shares`, which is the fraction of would-be `copy_from` users
who choose the new method:

```python
intv = fp.add_method(
    year         = 2010,
    copy_from    = 'inj',
    method_pars  = dict(name='dmpasc', label='DMPA-SC', efficacy=0.983),
    split_shares = 0.40,  # 40% of would-be injectable users switch
)
```

## Check what happened

Method usage is in `method_mix`, indexed by each method's `idx`:

```python
cm = sim.connectors.contraception
fp_mod = sim.people.fp
share = fp_mod.method_mix[cm.methods['dmpasc'].idx, -1] * 100
print(f'DMPA-SC share at end: {share:.1f}%')
```

Note `sim.people.fp` for the FP module and `sim.connectors.contraception` for the choice
module -- these live in different places.

For complete worked examples, see `examples/example_add_method.py` and
`examples/example_dmpasc.py` in the repository.
